holidays.name: National Pastry Day
holidays.description: A flaky, buttery day devoted to croissants, danishes, turnovers, eclairs, and every other layered or filled baked treat. Bakeries and home bakers alike are encouraged to treat themselves.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food observance that grew out of food-calendar listings and bakery promotions. There is no single documented founder, and it is often listed alongside other December baking-themed days.
holidays.funFact: Croissants are often associated with France, but they descend from the Austrian kipferl, a crescent-shaped pastry that was brought to Paris in the 1830s by an Austrian baker.

holidays.name: International Anti-Corruption Day
holidays.description: A global day for shining a light on bribery, shady deals, and backroom handshakes, and for encouraging transparency and honest governance everywhere.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated it in 2003, the same year it adopted the UN Convention against Corruption. The date of December 9 was chosen to mark the opening of that treaty for signature in Merida, Mexico.
holidays.funFact: The UN Convention against Corruption was the first legally binding global anti-corruption instrument, and it has been ratified by well over 180 parties.

holidays.name: Weary Willie Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the famous sad-faced hobo clown created by Emmett Kelly, who made audiences laugh by being melancholy, sweeping up spotlights, and trying to sweep away the circus's troubles.
holidays.origin: Emmett Kelly, the clown behind the Weary Willie character, was born on December 9, 1898, in Sedan, Kansas. The day is an informal circus-lover's observance honoring his birthday and his legacy.
holidays.funFact: One of Weary Willie's most famous bits was trying to sweep up a circle of light from a spotlight, and the light would just keep escaping the broom.

holidays.name: Santa Claus Day (Dutch Sinterklaas Eve Season Celebration)
holidays.description: An early-December gift-giving observance in which Santa and his predecessors visit with treats, rhymes, and small surprises, long before the Christmas rush.
holidays.origin: Rooted in the traditions of Saint Nicholas, which are celebrated across Europe in early December, with Sinterklaas arriving by boat in the Netherlands in November and gifts traded on December 5 or 6. In the U.S., some towns, such as Santa Claus, Indiana, host festivities around early December.
holidays.funFact: The name Santa Claus comes from the Dutch Sinterklaas, which came from Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop who was known for secret gifts.

holidays.name: Christmas Card Day
holidays.description: A day to dig out the pens, stamps, and glitter and send holiday cards to friends and family, preferably before the postal service gets swamped.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance tied to the history of the Christmas card, which was invented in London in 1843 by Sir Henry Cole. It falls in early-to-mid December, when card sending traditionally peaks.
holidays.funFact: The very first commercial Christmas card, commissioned by Henry Cole in 1843, caused a bit of a scandal because it showed a family happily drinking wine, including children.
